title: fix: classify text content-policy rejections as 4xx
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Classifies Gemini/OpenRouter PROHIBITED_CONTENT rejections as unbilled 422 errors using the existing content-policy detector; no fallback on policy refusals.
- Reads numeric error.code from successful HTTP error envelopes and preserves provider details. Provider credentials/capacity failures remain retryable.
- Records streamed policy failures as 422 in generation health, not server-error events. Already-started streams retain HTTP 200 and the original error body.
- Tests: 128 targeted tests pass across client, tracking, fallback, and error-observability suites; TypeScript and Biome pass.

gist.headline: Policy refusals find their lane
gist.blurb: The text gateway now recognizes a content-policy “no” for what it is, rather than sending it wandering through fallback machinery. Policy rejections stay unbilled, clearly labeled, and pleasantly unsurprising.
gist.summary: Gemini and OpenRouter PROHIBITED_CONTENT responses are now detected as unbilled 422 content-policy errors with provider details preserved, while credential and capacity failures remain retryable and streamed policy failures are tracked separately from server errors.
gist.impact: Text API users now receive clear 422 policy responses without fallback attempts or billing, and generation health records distinguish policy refusals from actual server failures.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy API garden has a clearly marked “422” garden gate that gently redirects prohibited-content notes into a compost bin rather than the emergency fallback tunnel. Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, reads the provider error label while a helpful CRT monitor robot updates a healthy garden ledger; code-plants and flowers show that the system remains calm and correctly sorted.
